children: OPEC+ will keep its oil production targets unchanged in November as the war involving Iran continues to disrupt supplies from several major producers and pushes crude prices toward $100 a barrel.
A seven-country group led by Saudi Arabia and Russia agreed Sunday to maintain existing quotas next month, continuing a previously announced pause in production increases through the end of 2026.

The decision comes as disruptions in the Persian Gulf have reduced production from Saudi Arabia, Iraq and Kuwait to well below prewar levels. The supply squeeze has helped lift crude prices while diesel prices have reached records, prompting Group of Seven nations to release emergency oil and fuel reserves.

OPEC+ had gradually increased quotas during the six months through August, reversing some of the production cuts introduced in 2023. Much of that additional capacity hasn't reached the market because the conflict has prevented several producers from pumping at their targeted levels.

For energy investors, OPEC+'s decision leaves geopolitical disruptions rather than official production quotas as the dominant force affecting near-term oil supply. If Persian Gulf output remains constrained, crude prices could stay elevated even without further OPEC+ cuts. Conversely, an easing of the conflict could bring significant production back to market and put downward pressure on prices.

The group also faces a longer-term decision over whether to restore another tranche of production that was removed from the market in 2022. Any increase will depend partly on an audit of members' actual production capacity, which could determine how future quotas are distributed.

The seven countries are scheduled to meet again Nov. 1 to consider December production levels. The full OPEC+ group will meet Nov. 29 to establish policy for 2027, making that meeting a key event for investors watching the outlook for global oil supply and prices.

title: OPEC+ holds November oil output targets steady amid supply squeeze
